knowledge:
- key_parameters: estim=Logical indicating whether to estimate the weight and path coefficients ;; path.test=Logical indicating whether to perform permutation tests for the significance of path coefficients ;; path=A two-column matrix specifying a subset of path coefficients to test, where each row contains the indices of two latent variables (if NULL, all paths are tested) ;; nperm=The number of permutations to use in the permutation test ;; latent.names=A character vector containing the names of the latent variables
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use when you want to perform a pathway-based association study to test the joint effects of multiple genotypes (grouped into genes) on multiple traits (grouped into clinical pathways) using structural equation modeling.
- pitfalls: Running the GSCA function twice on the same dataset may result in flipped signs of the parameter estimates (e.g., negative weights and negative path coefficients) due to the alternating least-squares algorithm, though the biological interpretation remains identical. Permutation testing is computationally intensive and can take several hours for large datasets with many permutations.

workflows.name: gsca_association_analysis
workflows.intent: Model and test the association between multiple genotypes and multiple traits using Generalized Structured Component Analysis (GSCA).
input: QCAHS1 (data.frame containing columns for genotypes/SNPs and clinical traits/phenotypes for each individual)
W0 (matrix of 0s and 1s mapping observed variables to latent variables)
B0 (matrix of 0s and 1s mapping latent variables to other latent variables)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare the genotype and trait data frame ;; 2. Define the latent variables and construct the W0 and B0 matrices ;; 3. Run GSCA to estimate weights and path coefficients, and/or perform permutation tests for path significance ;; 4. Extract significant gene-pathway associations from the resulting p-values
workflows.code:
library(ASGSCA)
data("QCAHS")
colnames(QCAHS)
QCAHS1=data.frame(QCAHS$TaqIB,QCAHS$HindIII,QCAHS$G1302A,QCAHS$G1564A,QCAHS$G308A,QCAHS$G238A,
QCAHS$HDL,QCAHS$LDL,QCAHS$APOB,QCAHS$TG,QCAHS$Glucose,QCAHS$Insulin)
ObservedVar=c("TaqIB","HindIII","G1302A","G1564A","G308A","G238A","HDL","LDL","APOB",
"TG","Glucose","Insulin")
colnames(QCAHS1)=ObservedVar
LatentVar=c("CETP","LPL","PGC","TNFa","Lipid metabolism","Energy metabolism")
W0=matrix(rep(0,12*6),nrow=12,ncol=6, dimnames=list(ObservedVar,LatentVar))
W0[1,1]=W0[2,2]=W0[3:4,3]=W0[5:6,4]=W0[7:10,5]=W0[8:12,6]=1
B0=matrix(rep(0,6*6),nrow=6,ncol=6, dimnames=list(LatentVar,LatentVar))
B0[1:3,5]=B0[3:4,6]=1
W0
B0
GSCA(QCAHS1,W0, B0,latent.names=LatentVar, estim=TRUE,path.test=FALSE,path=NULL,nperm=1000)
set.seed(2)
GSCA(QCAHS1,W0, B0,latent.names=LatentVar, estim=TRUE,path.test=TRUE,path=NULL,nperm=1000)
set.seed(2)
GSCA(QCAHS1,W0, B0,latent.names=LatentVar,estim=FALSE,path.test=TRUE,path=NULL,nperm=1000)
set.seed(2)
path0=matrix(c(2,3,5,6),ncol=2)
path0
GSCA(QCAHS1,W0, B0,latent.names=LatentVar, estim=FALSE,path.test=TRUE,path=path0,
nperm=1000)
data("ResQCAHS")
indices <- which(ResQCAHS$pvalues<0.05, arr.ind=TRUE)
ind.row=indices[,1] ; ind.col=indices[,2]
Significant<- matrix(rep(0,nrow(indices)*3),ncol=3);colnames(Significant)=c("Gene", "Pathway", "pval")
Significant[,1] <- rownames(ResQCAHS$pvalues)[ind.row]
Significant[,2] <- colnames(ResQCAHS$pvalues)[ind.col]
Significant[,3]<-ResQCAHS$pvalues[indices]
Significant
